ranked.headline: Logical teleportation, mediated T gates and transversal CZs target fault-tolerant control
ranked.summary: A lattice-surgery logical teleportation experiment on 41 superconducting qubits lands alongside proposals for color-code T gates, ion CZs and Rydberg CCZs.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is implementing logical and multi-qubit entangling operations across hardware platforms. Experimentally, logical qubits are teleported via lattice surgery between distance-three surface-code patches on 41 superconducting qubits. The proposals address other fault-tolerance bottlenecks. A persistent-mediator architecture reuses a 3D color-code block to apply repeated logical T gates to a 2D register, with simulations. In a double-well trapped-ion architecture, parallel transversal CZ gates act across neighboring wells, combined with dynamical decoupling and crosstalk mitigation. A reset-assisted scheme uses noisy mediator qubits to drive high-fidelity gates on long-lived data qubits, analyzed with quantum trajectories. For neutral atoms, an analytically specified CCZ gate under finite Rydberg interactions is compared with a fast antiblockade scheme. Separately, an analog Rydberg simulator performs phase estimation of ground-state energies and gaps for up to 19 atoms via Loschmidt echoes. Peripheral items cover Krotov control of GHZ-type XXZ states, bosonic Fock-state stabilization, an Fe2+:forsterite qubit and Majorana-based reservoir computing.

ranked.headline: Faster exact classical samplers for noisy and error-corrected quantum circuits
ranked.summary: Several preprints extend exact noisy-circuit sampling to near-Clifford QEC, coherent noise, mid-circuit measurements and general Kraus channels.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is classical machinery for sampling noisy quantum circuits, with error-correction workloads as the main target. MASQ is an exact measurement-adaptive sampler for near-Clifford QEC circuits that materializes only the non-Clifford contributions relevant to measurements. Compiled Clifford-augmented matrix product states accelerate coherent-noise QEC simulation and reach distance-9 surface codes. Pre-trajectory sampling with batched GPU execution is generalized to mid-circuit measurements and arbitrary Kraus channels while remaining exact. A second strand treats quantum hardware or circuits as samplers. One study quantifies how physical qubit embeddings affect annealer sampling of the 2D Ising model and feeds QPU-learned proposals into corrected Monte Carlo. Another trains a hypernetwork mapping Hamiltonian parameters to circuit angles for ground-state samplers. A third finds the Fisher trace uninformative for certifying Born machines and shows that kernel verdicts depend on tolerance. Peripheral items cover noisy Grover stopping thresholds, commutator-guided repair of shallow circuits, and Koopman-von Neumann flow simulation with surface-code estimates.

ranked.headline: Fast, accurate decoders and optimized syndrome circuits target practical qLDPC codes
ranked.summary: New qLDPC decoders report sub-microsecond latency and gains over BP+OSD, BP-LSD and Relay-BP, alongside circuit-scheduling and code-design advances.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is decoding under real-time constraints, increasingly for qLDPC codes rather than only surface codes. SCOPE, a physics-informed parallel decoder, reports a logical error rate of 4.82e-10 on the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle code with 173.8 ns latency. TEMPO-BP adapts per-variable memory strength via local feedback and lowers failure rates relative to BP+OSD and Relay-BP. TCBP-JOBS runs on GPUs, learns calibrated fault probabilities and matches Tesseract accuracy. A hybrid sliding-window decoder for trapped-ion noise models uses soft-output confidence to switch windows and improves on BP-LSD. For surface codes, Beyond Blossom reports a 4.23x geometric-mean speedup for CPU MWPM via local predecoding. A second strand optimizes syndrome-extraction circuits: Proxima schedules them using a DEM-based proximity metric, and structure-guided CP-SAT synthesis reduces logical error rates. Code-design work adds Armillary codes with rates above 1/2 for fixed-connectivity superconducting hardware and rate-optimal distance-3 and distance-4 color codes.

ranked.headline: Simulations calibrate lensing, redshift and assembly-bias systematics in structure probes
ranked.summary: New preprints quantify n(z) and lens-multipole biases on w0wa and H0, and trace halo and galaxy secondary bias with TNG300 and DESI-BGS mocks.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of simulations to quantify systematics and secondary dependencies that link observables to cosmological parameters. On nuisance modelling, on-the-fly Gaussian Process reconstruction of n(z) for Euclid-like 3×2pt analyses shows that redshift-distribution systematics bias w0wa. IllustrisTNG ellipticals indicate that multipole mass terms bias time-delay H0 by 1–6%. On secondary bias, TNG300 shows that the unbound matter fraction in the circum-halo medium largely explains halo secondary bias, through cold tidal and hot inertial accretion regimes. Luminosity-weighted marked correlations are proposed as a null test for galaxy assembly bias and are tested on DESI-BGS mocks at 0.1<z<0.4. Two papers compare observations directly with simulations. SDSS genus topology agrees much better with modern galaxy models in HR4 than with earlier ones. HESTIA comparisons find an excess of close Milky Way satellite pairs. More peripheral items cover a GR test using DESI Legacy Imaging cluster clustering, Gini-index BCG dominance, and Euclid Q1 radio-loud AGN fractions.

ranked.headline: Real-time decoders and control hardware co-designed to meet QEC latency bounds
ranked.summary: FPGA neural decoding below a microsecond, 1 μs Pauli-frame feedback, and multi-GPU relay-BP decoding treat real-time QEC latency as a hardware design target.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is co-design of the classical hardware that must keep pace with fault-tolerant quantum processors. On decoding, Rapids pairs a streaming neural decoder with FPGAs to decode surface-code syndromes in under a microsecond, with lower logical error rates than existing decoders. Pêlagos distributes relay belief-propagation decoding across multiple GPUs under real-time constraints, and a survey organizes hierarchical decoding by decoder- and code-level hierarchy, platform and latency trade-offs. CHEQ evaluates decoders concurrently on an FPGA using geometric-skip circuit-level noise sampling, matching Stim firing rates within 0.16%. QuFrame's control microarchitecture closes the QEC loop within 1 μs via real-time Pauli frame tracking. A second strand addresses platform-specific compilation and control: NEAT for AOD transport in neutral-atom arrays, an FPGA quantum data processing unit that cuts assembly latency, Lean-verified QCCD co-design (QCCDCert) scaling to 512 qubits, and MLIR-based circuit cutting (QWeaver). Common to these is treating latency and hardware constraints as primary design targets.

ranked.headline: DESI-era tests of evolving dark energy span model comparison, reconstruction and SN Ia systematics
ranked.summary: Eight preprints in mid-November test departures from a cosmological constant with DESI, CMB, supernova and lensing data, and probe the supernova systematics behind them.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is whether DESI BAO or full-shape data, combined with CMB, supernovae and lensing, support dark energy that departs from a cosmological constant. Model-level work compares one-parameter vacuum histories within VCDM, where F42 is favored by AIC with supernovae. A DESI DR1 full-shape analysis finds the scalar-field Fading Dark Sector model outperforming CPL w0-wa. Two non-parametric reconstructions of dark-energy density and gravitational response report a phantom-divide crossing near z≈0.5–0.7, one also testing whether dark energy clusters. A generalised axion-like quintessence model is confronted with multiple probes. The LEMAITRE project and a ZTF/SNLS/HSC calibration proposal aim at independent SN Ia constraints. A 0i Einstein-equation proposal offers observable-only tests of dark-sector degeneracies.

ranked.headline: Symmetry and structure exploited to cut resources in quantum and classical many-body simulation
ranked.summary: Eight preprints use spin symmetry, sparsity and structured hardware models to reduce sampling, circuit and classical simulation costs, with several run on devices.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is using symmetry or problem structure to reduce resource costs in many-body simulation. Spin-adapted SqDRIFT completes sampled configurations to enforce S^2 symmetry and yield exact spin eigenstates, while a loading circuit prepares U(1)×SU(2)-symmetric MPS from spin-adapted reduced tensors for fault-tolerant algorithms. Sparse quantum prolate diagonalization uses compressed sensing to lower sample complexity from O(N_s) to O(log N_s) and is demonstrated on trapped ions. Gutzwiller embedding for quench dynamics and RG-guided variational circuits on a 16-qubit IQM device likewise encode physical structure. Quantum-walk search on complete bipartite graphs is realized on a gate-based processor. On the classical side, F2-linear partitioning scales Pauli propagation beyond 10^11 strings, and an effective Hamiltonian method models 96-transmon quench dynamics.

ranked.headline: Noise structure on superconducting hardware is being measured and fed into QEC decoding and calibration
ranked.summary: Preprints tie measured noise on superconducting processors to surface-code stability, calibration, magic states and simulation of loss and leakage.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is confronting non-ideal noise in error-corrected and error-mitigated computation on superconducting devices. A 105-qubit experiment extends surface-code stability tests to 7x7 patches and identifies temporally correlated heating-to-|3> leakage. Magic state cultivation with lattice-surgery escapes is implemented on IBM hardware. Supporting work includes GEARS, which uses gate-error amplification with syndrome feedback to recalibrate during QEC and reduces measurement needs about eightfold, and a method that predicts logical error rates and selects rectangular surface-code geometries under biased circuit-level noise. Ellis, a Pauli-frame simulator, handles qubit loss and leakage. Near-term items extend bnZNE mitigation to randomized circuits and propose a noise-aware testing oracle with a controlled false-positive rate. The common novelty is linking characterized noise structure to calibration, resource choices and validation.

ranked.headline: Compilers and verified tools couple resource optimization with correctness guarantees for fault tolerance
ranked.summary: Eight preprints pair optimized compilation and fault-tolerant design with Lean-verified or exact certification of circuits and stabilizer codes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is software infrastructure for fault-tolerant quantum computing in which resource optimization is paired with correctness guarantees. Compilation work includes MARBLE, which synthesizes OpenQASM block-encoding circuits from matrix formulas, qlin, which rewrites dynamic-circuit branches and decoders to reduce waiting latency with a Lean 4-verified translation validator, and PRISM, which keeps multiple logical-gate realizations open during routing for dual-rail qubits. Verification work includes a formally verified Shor order-finding harness at O(n^(2+ε)) gate cost, QECLean for machine-verified code specification, and QEDist for exact stabilizer-code distance certification. Architecture-level papers formalize reaction depth, with constant-depth coherent Boolean arithmetic, and use Block Checks with Pareto tree search for state preparation. Not every item involves formal verification.

ranked.headline: Theory links hidden magnetic order to optical, spin-transport and magnon responses
ranked.summary: Eight preprints propose symmetry-sensitive probes and magnon-based functionalities in altermagnets, spin-nematics, noncoplanar and multiferroic magnets.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is theoretical identification of measurable responses that expose or exploit unconventional magnetic order. For altermagnets and noncoplanar antiferromagnets, octupolar magneto-optical effects are proposed as field-free probes, and nonlinear spin generation and spin photocurrent as probes of spin-space symmetry, domains and quantum geometry. Twist engineering of collinear bilayers is proposed to yield quasicrystalline altermagnets with high-order spin polarization. On the magnon side, single magnons and bound magnon pairs in pyrochlore spin-nematics give competing Berry-curvature thermal Hall contributions with field-tunable sign reversal; CrI3 nanotubes in an axial field acquire a conical phase and a large pseudo-orbital magnon moment; and gated domain boundaries in BiFeO3 modulate nonreciprocal magnons in a proposed transistor. Cavity photon condensation from scalar spin chirality and defect-enhanced orbital magnetoelectric responses are more peripheral. All items are preprints.

ranked.headline: Correlation structure and non-Hermitian spectra control monitored and dissipative quantum dynamics
ranked.summary: Seven preprints from 12–18 November tie correlations and exceptional points to non-Markovianity, sensing, monitored circuits and squeezing.
ranked.synthesis: The main thread is how correlation structure and non-Hermitian spectral features shape open, monitored or symmetry-constrained quantum systems. Exceptional points are defined at the quantum-channel level in a driven-dissipative Kerr-cat qubit, where they map a Markovian–non-Markovian phase diagram and allow switching between regimes. A separate proposal uses reservoir engineering in particle-hole Nambu space with a common reservoir to give exceptional-point sensing a quantum-metrological advantage. In hybrid measurement-unitary circuits, trajectory and projected-state ensembles undergo ensemble phase transitions at the measurement-induced point. Correlation diagnostics form a related strand: Gaussian ergotropy of two oscillator detectors probes spatial correlations that distinguish accelerated vacuum from a thermal field, and ground-state spin squeezing in Z2-symmetric models is linked to collective excitation gaps. Symmetry-preserving variational circuit design and Rydberg-array annealing analysis are less directly connected.

ranked.headline: Forecasts and new statistics gauge whether 21-cm, CMB, lensing and PTA data can separate LCDM from alternatives
ranked.summary: Seven preprints from 12-19 November 2026 forecast how well upcoming 21-cm, CMB, time-delay and pulsar timing data can test LCDM and its alternatives.
ranked.synthesis: Most items assess how well forthcoming or existing datasets can discriminate LCDM from alternatives, relying on forecasts and new statistics rather than new measurements. For 21-cm data, persistent homology on Cosmic Dawn brightness maps, the phase gradient spectrum for the squeezed bispectrum, and SKA1-Low forecasts for boosted dark matter each target distinct observables. Bayesian forecasts for Simons Observatory and CMB-S4 examine whether w0waCDM can be separated from LCDM shadow models. The time-delay forecast finds that mass-sheet transformation uncertainties reduce the significance of the decreasing H0 trend to ~1σ. The binaryfog surrogate tests how astrophysical priors affect evidence for new-physics sources in pulsar timing arrays. The Shapley jet-alignment result, at 4.5σ, is a separate observational large-scale-structure claim.

ranked.headline: Emulators, differentiable codes and alternative probes are prepared for survey-era cosmological inference
ranked.summary: Hi-COLA, bihalofit-JAX and a Lyman-alpha EFT forward model supply fast, survey-ready modeling, while DESI DR2 and FRB analyses test GR and constrain Ωm and w.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is modeling infrastructure for upcoming survey analyses. A Hi-COLA-trained emulator targets the nonlinear matter power spectrum in Cubic Galileon gravity for LSST Year 1 weak lensing and clustering. bihalofit-JAX provides a differentiable, open-source nonlinear bispectrum code with projected statistics, reported to run orders of magnitude faster than alternatives. A cubic-order EFT forward model of the Lyman-alpha forest, validated on CAMELS and Sherwood, yields BAO shift predictions and simulation-based priors. A secondary thread applies alternative probes: a physics-informed neural network reconstructs the dark energy equation of state and growth index from DESI DR2 and other data to test GR, and fast radio bursts are used to map cosmic baryons with IllustrisTNG and to infer Ωm and w from 125 localized bursts alone. The QCD equation-of-state study of early-universe expansion and the stochastic gravitational-wave spectrum is peripheral to this thread.

ranked.headline: Cosmological inference is being scaled through posterior reuse, GPU samplers and validated survey pipelines
ranked.summary: New preprints pair faster samplers and survey pipelines with validation on simulations and community comparisons ahead of LISA, LSST, Euclid and SKA data.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is computational infrastructure for cosmological inference on forthcoming datasets, with validation as a companion theme. ASPIRE reuses existing posteriors for joint dark-siren cosmological and population inference, reporting 6-28x speedups over reanalysis. samsara++ provides a C++/CUDA trans-dimensional MCMC sampler for LISA global fits with overlapping Galactic binaries and noise. The LSST DESC cluster pipeline is validated on cosmoDC2 mocks, constraining Omega_c and sigma_8 from cluster counts. Euclid work addresses machine-learning components: strong-lens detection depends strongly on training-set composition, image format and ensembling, while EuclidFM learns 128-dim embeddings from Q1 photometry. SKA SDC3b compares 16 teams' EoR pipelines and reports inter-team variability. The items span different probes and do not all address sampler efficiency.

ranked.headline: Optical and electrical stimuli write and read textures in compensated and antiferromagnetic systems
ranked.summary: Six preprints from 12–17 November 2026 show optical and electrical writing of skyrmions and compensated states, alongside probes of antiferromagnetic switching.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is deterministic writing of magnetic order with ultrafast optical or electrical stimuli. Picosecond circularly polarized pulses write fixed-chirality Néel skyrmions in Co/Pt, with chirality set by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Laser pulses imprint antiferromagnetic skyrmions in a coupled ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic bilayer within picoseconds. Atomistic simulations find all-optical helicity-independent switching in GdCo with as little as 1.5 at.% Gd. In artificial spin ice, spin-orbit torque switching and planar Hall readout address a compensated state electrically. Pulsed-field MOKE on Fe2Mo3O8 (metamagnetism) and NV magnetometry of thermally activated switching in CrPS4 trilayers are probe-oriented studies that connect more loosely, addressing antiferromagnetic response and bistability.

ranked.headline: Euclid DR1 documentation sets out survey coverage, photometry validation and galaxy property pipelines
ranked.summary: Five Euclid DR1 papers appeared on 12 November 2026, documenting the release contents, survey coverage, masks, photometry validation and PHZ galaxy properties.
ranked.synthesis: The items form a coordinated documentation set for Euclid Data Release 1 rather than a set of cosmological analyses. The overview describes a two-part release of images, spectra and catalogues covering about a billion objects from wide and deep fields, while the survey paper reports 2100 deg² of Wide Survey area. Supporting papers describe the photometric masks, which trace spatial variations in survey properties, and the PHZ pipeline, which applies NNPZ nearest-neighbour inference with a COSMOS reference sample to derive non-cosmological galaxy properties. The main quantified check is the multi-band photometry comparison with the JWST-based COSMOS2025 catalogue, where median offsets are mostly within 10% and largest in NIR deep model-fitting. None of the items presents cosmological results.

ranked.headline: Machine learning links dark-matter structure to galaxy and gas observables in both directions
ranked.summary: Five preprints use simulation-trained models to populate DMO halos with galaxies or to infer mass and gas fields from observations, from z~2.3 to z>6.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of simulation-trained or empirical models to connect dark matter structure with baryonic observables. In the forward direction, Extremely Randomized Trees and Gaussian Processes populate the 2.8 Gpc FLAMINGO-10k dark-matter-only run with a galaxy catalogue, while an empirical model predicts individual halo concentrations from assembly histories in CDM and WDM over z=0-5. A flexible model linking halo mass, stellar mass, SFR and UV magnitude is fit to JWST UV luminosity functions and angular correlations at z>6. In the inverse direction, deep learning recovers cluster mass maps and subhalo substructure from HST imaging, matching CLASH lensing, and a CNN reconstructs IGM column-density maps from noisy KCWI Lyα cubes of z~2.3 protoclusters. The new element is the breadth of redshift and observable coverage, though items differ in method and target.

ranked.headline: Theory models of tracer cross-spectra are validated against simulations ahead of survey analyses
ranked.summary: Five preprints test EFT and halo-model descriptions of Lyα, 21 cm, SPHEREx, CMB lensing and tSZ tracers on simulations before application to data.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is validating theoretical descriptions of tracer auto- and cross-correlations on simulations. Two Lyman-alpha works test effective field theory: a minimal tree-level EFT for 21 cm and Lyα auto- and cross-spectra at z=2.4-4.2 that constrains HI and Lyα biases, and a full-shape power spectrum and bispectrum analysis validated on AbacusSummit mocks at z=2.5 for DESI. The SPHEREx pair forecasts cross-correlations of extragalactic background light with CMB lensing, and the second paper reports halo-model predictions matching lightcone simulations. The baryonification paper presents two ways to build thermal SZ Compton-y maps from dark-matter-only lightcones. The new element is simulation-level checking spanning line-intensity, forest, lensing and SZ observables.

ranked.headline: Material- and geometry-defined resonances give tunable control in metasurfaces, microresonators and nanoantennas
ranked.summary: Five November 2026 preprints quantify tunable resonant light control across BIC metasurfaces, coupled microresonators and plasmonic nanoantennas.
ranked.synthesis: The preprints share a focus on setting optical response through resonance design in structured media, with tunability as the recurring theme. A silicon BIC metasurface uses strong QBIC-GMR coupling to reach intrinsic circular dichroism of 0.995 with Q of 1083 at 1653.9 nm. MAPbBr3 BIC metasurfaces are tuned reversibly and continuously by HCl/HBr vapor anion exchange. Coupled TiO2 and perovskite-coated microresonators show tunable whispering gallery mode hybridization. In plasmonics, nanoantenna arrays with hollow-core fiber coupling provide polarization-resilient THz generation and detection, with 2.1 mW output and 145 dB dynamic range. A coaxial nanoantenna study maps inverse Faraday magnetization across Au, Ag, Cu, Al and TiN. Platforms and spectral ranges differ, but each work reports quantified control of resonant behavior through material choice, coupling or environment.

ranked.headline: Computational correction of measurement errors and bottlenecks in structured-light imaging
ranked.summary: Five preprints address specific error sources and resource limits in turbulence transmission, single-pixel imaging, ptychography and hyperspectral microscopy.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is recovering optical field information from constrained or imperfect measurements through computation or engineered illumination and readout. Active convolved illumination is reviewed as a means of preserving mode structure through turbulent media using segmented reciprocal-space control. Two single-pixel imaging preprints treat measurement imperfections differently: a Fourier-domain response-matrix correction addresses quantization errors in binary-encoded Fourier acquisition, while a calibration and composite-readout framework converts temporal mixing into a measurement resource. A stochastic gradient descent framework for X-ray ptychography reduces peak GPU memory to 65% and time to 22% versus the comparison method. Event-camera Fourier-transform hyperspectral microscopy with continuous birefringent interferometer scanning reaches real-time widefield spectral acquisition. Modalities differ; the novelty lies in targeted treatment of specific error sources or resource bottlenecks within each.

ranked.headline: Magnetic, ferroelectric and optical order switch valley and exciton states in 2D
ranked.summary: Five preprints report electrical, magnetic and optical switching of valley and exciton properties in WSe2 and WS2 van der Waals systems.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is external control of excitonic and valley properties in van der Waals materials through an ordered degree of freedom. In WS2/CrSBr heterostructures, type-II band alignment, magnetic-proximity Zeeman valley splitting and spin-selective interlayer charge transfer couple valley and magnetic excitons. In WSe2/CrPS4, a light-controlled Néel vector switches valley polarization optically via spin-polarized charge transfer. In rhombohedrally stacked bilayer WSe2, sliding ferroelectricity gives hysteretic, electrically switchable exciton photoluminescence and Raman response, and in few-layer R-stacked WSe2 it switches dipolar exciton transport and drives dipole reconfiguration toward quadrupolar excitons. The NbOCl2 preprint reports room-temperature antiferroelectricity with reversible switching to a ferroelectric state, probed by SHG, but does not address valley or exciton states directly. What is new is the range of switchable order parameters, magnetic, ferroelectric and optical, used as handles on valley and exciton states.

ranked.headline: Disorder reshapes Chern plateaus, orbital Hall currents and Weyl magnetotransport
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show that disorder, rather than being neglected, controls plateau widths, orbital Hall response and anisotropic magnetotransport.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread across these four preprints is that disorder serves as an active source of transport response, not a perturbation to be neglected. In twisted bilayer MoTe2 Chern insulators, layer-dependent disorder is reported to shape the widths and transitions of integer and fractional Hall plateaus. A Kubo-Bastin Chebyshev study of a centrosymmetric sp3 tight-binding square lattice examines how the quadrupole-origin orbital Hall effect responds to disorder and how it can be tuned. A generalized semiclassical Boltzmann analysis of multi-Weyl semimetals goes beyond constant relaxation time, incorporating orbital moment and intervalley scattering with monopole charge N as a parameter. The newest item extends this picture: structural and electrostatic disorder, including in amorphous graphene, generates sizable orbital Hall currents absent in pristine systems. What is new is the emphasis on orbital Hall currents arising from disorder itself, rather than only modifying clean-limit responses.

ranked.headline: Non-sinusoidal Josephson junctions are engineered as nonlinear elements for qubits
ranked.summary: Four preprints from November 2026 examine Josephson junctions whose current-phase relation departs from the ideal sinusoid for qubit use.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is treating Josephson junction transport as a design variable rather than assuming an ideal sinusoidal current-phase relation. A proposal for noise-protected superconducting qutrits uses the second harmonic of the current-phase relation in three-junction loops, with altermagnetic elements. A study of Al/AlOx/Al tunnel junctions examines non-ergodic area scaling of Andreev transport against the sinusoidal assumption. Gatemon work reports in-situ ternary InAsSb/Al nanowire junctions with gate tunability over GHz and coherent control, with T1 of about 0.2-1 us. A study of planar Ge Josephson junctions finds gate-tunable spin splitting for Andreev spin qubits that is independent of junction width, unlike InAs. What is new is the set of materials platforms and deliberate departures from conventional junction behavior, though the studies differ in maturity and scope.

ranked.headline: Exactly solvable lattice models reveal exceptional spectra and localization
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply exact solvability to non-Hermitian, disordered and hyperbolic lattice models, probing exceptional points and localization.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is exact or analytically controlled analysis of lattice models whose spectra or localization depart from Hermitian, translation-invariant expectations. An exactly solvable non-Hermitian Kitaev chain with unequal pairing amplitudes shows an exceptional point where many-body energies collapse, together with Lifshitz criticality. Non-Hermitian fermionic chains with random imaginary gauge fields display erratic skin localization and density fragmentation into Fermi domains. A disordered spin-1 chain with an exact binary-tree Fock-space structure rigorously bounds spreading at strong disorder. The three-colored Kitaev model is studied on finite hyperbolic periodic-boundary clusters through ground-state flux sectors and two-vison gaps. The new element is the combination of exact solvability with diagnostics of exceptional spectra, fragmentation and localization across non-Hermitian, disordered and hyperbolic-geometry settings.

ranked.headline: Engineered photonic lattices control flat bands, BICs, and mobility edges
ranked.summary: Recent preprints tie coupling sign, non-Hermiticity, and lattice geometry to flatband and edge-state localization in photonic systems.
ranked.synthesis: Across these four preprints, engineered photonic structures are used to control how optical modes are localized or confined: flat bands, bound states in the continuum (BICs), mobility edges, and edge states. Two items are model-based. One is a four-mode non-Hermitian model of C2-symmetric photonic-crystal slabs in which coupling sign governs BIC merging and flatband formation, with reported Q scaling as k^-6. The other is a one-dimensional non-Hermitian pseudospin lattice in which non-Hermiticity embeds compact localized states in a continuum. An experimental preprint reports exact mobility edges and flat-band states in a two-dimensional photonic quasicrystal realized with auxiliary subsystems and photonic waveguides. A fourth proposal addresses antihelical gapless edge states in a photonic metacrystal with staggered bianisotropy, so it concerns edge states rather than flat bands. The new element is explicit tuning of flatband and BIC physics via coupling sign and non-Hermiticity, alongside experimental verification of exact mobility edges in a photonic quasicrystal.

ranked.headline: Spectrally selective multilayer and metasurface designs for thermal energy conversion
ranked.summary: Numerical studies of selective emitters and absorbers, plus a new optical property database, target thermal-radiative energy conversion design.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is spectral control of thermal radiation, where wavelength-resolved absorption, emission and reflection determine energy conversion efficiency. A 16-layer MgO/Si multilayer on tungsten is inverse-designed as a selective emitter for GaSb thermophotovoltaic cells, with a modeled conversion efficiency of 47.0%. A gold-carbon metasurface uses a dielectric spacer to tune gap-mode overlap with carbon, sharpening the infrared roll-off in solar-thermal absorbers. The SpaderOptics database provides optical and thermal-radiative properties of 21 materials under the AM0 solar spectrum, offering property data relevant to absorber and emitter design. The photonic Maxwell's demon proposal is less directly tied to this design thread: it uses one-way dielectric mirrors and wavelength-converting materials in a 3D box to accumulate blackbody radiation. The new elements are inverse-design of a multilayer emitter, spacer-based gap-mode tuning, and a material property database under AM0 illumination. All four items are numerical or proposal-stage.

ranked.headline: Accidental BICs in photonic lattices and metasurfaces tie to parity and nonlocality
ranked.summary: Recent preprints refine accidental BIC theory via parity restoration and nonlocal scattering zeros, alongside Berry-phase studies of Möbius resonators.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the characterization of bound states in the continuum (BICs), localized modes that persist within the radiation continuum of open photonic systems. Two items address accidental BICs directly. One reports that in vertically asymmetric photonic lattices they are governed by radiation-source parity and recovered through radiation-source parity restoration. The other models metasurface BICs as converging reflection and transmission zeros and argues that accidental BICs require spatially nonlocal response. A third preprint studies Berry phase and topological quasi-bound states in Möbius resonators, reporting a mode-dependent phase. The fourth item, on hybrid graphene plasmon-silica phonon eigenmodes in a graphene ring, is a plasmonic system with quadrupolar eigenmodes forming multiband vortex states, and it is less directly tied to the BIC framing. The new element is the framing of accidental BIC existence in terms of parity and nonlocality.

ranked.headline: Wavefunction zeros and edge modes diagnose topological invariants beyond bulk spectra
ranked.summary: Recent preprints diagnose Chern, Z2 and Z invariants through overlap zeros, localizer operators and non-Hermitian Loschmidt matrices.
ranked.synthesis: The four preprints share a dominant thread: topological invariants and boundary-protected modes are diagnosed through quantities other than the conventional bulk Hamiltonian spectrum. Arxiv 2611.25037 reads relative Chern and Z2 invariants of two gapped band structures from zeros of the occupied-subspace overlap determinant. Arxiv 2611.25028 shows that crystalline symmetry can enforce wavefunction zeros and vorticities characterizing Chern topology, readable from band-dispersion shifts. Arxiv 2611.26160 generalizes the spectral localizer to unify Z and Z2 invariants for hinge modes, Dirac nodes and valley boundary modes. Arxiv 2611.19328 attributes boundary effects in dynamical quantum phase transitions to edge modes of the non-Hermitian Loschmidt matrix rather than Hamiltonian topology. The novelty lies in the shift of the diagnostic object toward overlap and wavefunction zeros, localizer operators and non-Hermitian Loschmidt matrices. The DQPT item is the least direct fit, since it concerns dynamics rather than ground-state band topology.

ranked.headline: Nonreciprocal, modulated, and tunable optical responses in compact photonic platforms
ranked.summary: Recent preprints report nonreciprocal, modulated, and tunable optical responses in 2D semiconductors, Floquet metasurfaces, and van der Waals magnonic cavities.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the engineering of optical response beyond static, reciprocal, linear behavior within compact geometries. Two items address nonreciprocity directly: a computational study of integrated isolators built from nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors that use spin-momentum locking, including an all-optical isolator proposal, and a Floquet metasurface of three closely spaced conducting sheets whose temporal modulation yields asymmetric frequency conversion, reported as violating Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation. A tripartite van der Waals cavity magnonic device with CrCl3 adds tunable coupling through hierarchical anti-crossing and reduced magnon loss in an experimental setting. An inverse-designed transparent conducting oxide cavity at the epsilon-near-zero point, studied theoretically, reports stronger confinement and faster dynamics. What is new is the joint control of nonreciprocity, modulation, and coupling in compact platforms. The items differ in method and maturity and do not share a single mechanism.

ranked.headline: Bilayer graphene spectra from q-deformed models and twisted-bilayer Monte Carlo
ranked.summary: Three November 2026 preprints revisit energy spectra in bilayer graphene and related few-body systems using deformed-algebra and quantum Monte Carlo methods.
ranked.synthesis: The common scientific thread is the computation of energy spectra in two-dimensional and few-body quantum systems. Two preprints address bilayer graphene directly. One derives spectra, currents, and thermodynamics for q-deformed Dirac oscillator models of monolayer and bilayer graphene in a magnetic field. The other applies momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo to twisted bilayer graphene, explicitly including remote bands and testing the validity of flat-band projection. The distinctive elements are the deformed-algebra treatment of the magnetic-field problem and the explicit assessment of interaction effects beyond projected flat-band models in the twisted case. A third preprint computes trion energy levels in bulk semiconductors across hole-to-electron mass ratios using finite-element and Gaussian expansion methods. It shares the spectral-calculation approach but not the graphene context.

ranked.headline: Programmable unitary interferometers for coherent photonic computing and measurement
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend programmable unitary photonic hardware to optical neural networks, modular tiling, and spectral measurement.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is programmable unitary interferometric circuits as the computational primitive for coherent photonic systems. Two preprints address unitary transformations directly: one proposes a logarithmic-depth butterfly interferometer architecture for parameter-efficient unitary transformations in coherent optical neural networks, and the other proposes a modular processor built from unitary tiles of fixed mixers and programmable phases, evaluated by numerical fitting. A third preprint applies the same kind of hardware differently, realizing a universal silicon photonic chip in which unequal path lengths between two 8x8 unitary circuits enable simultaneous spectral measurement and programmable filtering at 0.05 nm resolution. What is new is the joint emphasis on depth-efficient parameterization, modular tiling of unitary elements, and multifunctional use across computation and measurement.

ranked.headline: Resonant metasurfaces enhance UV harmonic generation and quantum-well SHG modeling
ranked.summary: Gold nano-pillar metasurfaces now reach UV and deep-UV harmonic generation, while plasmonic quantum-well SHG models add a formal treatment of the same platform class.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is nonlinear frequency conversion in engineered sub-wavelength structures. arxiv:2611.17037 reports experiments and full-vector simulations showing that resonant gold nano-pillar metasurfaces enhance second and third harmonic generation into the UV and deep-UV under ultrafast excitation. arxiv:2611.23943 offers a semi-analytical framework for second-harmonic generation in plasmonic metasurfaces with multiple quantum wells, addressing nonlinear current density, saturation, periodic SH boundary conditions, and the development of boundary conditions. arxiv:2611.24530 shares only the sub-wavelength grating design approach, using it to confine surface acoustic waves for a mid-infrared acousto-optic phase modulator at 460 MHz on GaAs/AlGaAs. What is new across the set is the experimental extension of resonant harmonic conversion into the UV regime and the formal modeling of metasurface SHG with quantum-well nonlinearities.
